title: Nesting & Hierarchy 🪆
description: How elements fit inside each other and why order matters.

slides.title: Parent and Child Elements 👨‍👧
slides.content:
# The Family Tree of Your Page When one element is inside another, we call them **parent** and **child**. ```html
  • Item 1
  • Item 2
``` - `
    ` is the parent, each `
  • ` is a child. - Elements at the same level (like the two `
  • `s) are **siblings**. This hierarchy is crucial for CSS and JavaScript to target elements.

slides.title: The Golden Rule of Nesting 🥇
slides.content: # Always Close in Reverse Order If you open `` then ``, you must close `` then ``. ❌ **Wrong:** `Click` ✅ **Correct:** `Click` Tags must never overlap like a Venn diagram. They nest like a set of Russian dolls.

quizData.question: Which of these is correctly nested?
quizData.explanation: The opening order (div then p) must match closing order (p then div).

slides.title: Indentation Reveals the Structure 🔍
slides.content:
# Make Nesting Visible Good indentation helps you and others read the code: ```html

Title

Some text with a bold part.

``` - Each nesting level adds 2 (or 4) spaces. - It instantly shows parent‑child relationships. - Most code editors can auto‑indent for you.

quizData.question: Indentation affects how the page is displayed in the browser.
quizData.explanation: Indentation is only for human readability. The browser ignores extra spaces and line breaks in the source.
